clue.text: George's firearm I found in bed

parts.note: an automatic is a self-loading gun

indicators.note: found in says the letter I sits inside the word for bed

parts.note: a plot is a garden bed

explanation.surface: Someone finds a gun hidden in their bed and asks if it belongs to George.
explanation.walkthrough: 'George' is slang among airmen for the autopilot of an aircraft; the 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Old RAF slang named the self-steering device on a plane George.

clue.text: Approaching Christmas, my days are numbered

definitions.text: Approaching Christmas, my days are numbered

parts.words: Approaching Christmas, my days are numbered
parts.note: a gloomy-sounding line spoken by an object whose December days carry numbered doors

explanation.surface: Someone or something fears its end is near as the festive season arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'My days are numbered' sounds like doom, but literally the item has days 1 to 24 printed on it.
explanation.definitionFit: A December countdown card with little numbered doors for each day before the twenty-fifth.

clue.text: Number with clever sound

parts.note: ten is a number
able means capable or clever

explanation.surface: A number paired with a word that sounds clever.
explanation.definitionFit: A sound argument is defensible, one that can be maintained against attack.

clue.text: Man supporting college principal's work of art

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting word sits below, so it comes second

parts.note: the head of some Oxford and Cambridge colleges is called the Master
a piece is a man in chess or draughts

explanation.surface: A man backing the head of a college's art.
explanation.walkthrough: A chessman is called a piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A supreme achievement in painting or sculpture is a great work of art.

clue.text: Little rascal's very difficult question head ignored

indicators.note: head ignored says the opening letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: a stinker is a very hard problem or question

explanation.surface: A cheeky child poses an awkward question.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A mischievous child can be called this, a British informal term for an imp.

clue.text: Incautious knight

definitions.meaning: a mounted soldier or Royalist horseman

explanation.definitionFit: The word means offhand or rash, and also a horseman, especially a Royalist in the English Civil War.

clue.text: Iris Murdoch's distinctive doctrine

indicators.note: distinctive here hints at a small marked-out part of the name, a run of letters within it

explanation.surface: The novelist Iris Murdoch had her own distinctive philosophy.
explanation.definitionFit: A suffix used as a noun for any distinctive theory or belief system.

clue.text: Sources at home penetrating first of oil rigs

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of oil
penetrating means getting inside the following letters

parts.note: in means at home

explanation.surface: Where oil comes from, drilled at home on rigs.
explanation.definitionFit: Beginnings or starting points are sources of something.

clue.text: Court officer upset as garments tear

indicators.note: upset suggests the three words are knocked over into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is distressed as their clothes rip.
explanation.definitionFit: An official who keeps order in a law court or legislature.

clue.text: Oven is only partially used for meat

indicators.note: partially says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A cooking tip: the oven is only partly needed when roasting meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Deer flesh is a meat eaten as game, so the phrase points to it as a kind of meat.

clue.text: A member after volume, one about horror story creature

indicators.note: after puts 'A member' behind the letter for volume

parts.note: MP is a Member of Parliament
I is the Roman numeral one
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A list of components builds up a monster from a horror tale.
explanation.definitionFit: Dracula is the classic bloodsucking undead figure of Gothic horror fiction.

clue.text: Arrest sailor following end of altercation

indicators.note: following places the sailor after that final letter
end of picks the final letter of the word altercation

parts.note: AB is an able seaman

explanation.surface: Police detain a sailor after a quarrel ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To nab someone is informal for to catch or seize them, as police do.

clue.text: Reveal awful pain is constant

indicators.note: awful suggests the word Reveal is mangled into a different order

parts.note: a sting is a sharp pain

explanation.surface: Telling someone about terrible pain that never lets up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awful' rearranges REVEAL to EVERLA; 'is' links wordplay to definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unending and perpetual is constant, never ceasing.

clue.text: Emblem of country's peerage lads vandalised

indicators.note: vandalised suggests the two words are smashed up into new order

explanation.surface: Young aristocrats deface a national symbol.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is' or 'has', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An eagle with wings and legs outspread is a heraldic national symbol, as on the US seal.

clue.text: Sinister member of the nobility over in Cyprus

indicators.note: in places the turned word inside the code for Cyprus

parts.note: CY is the international code for Cyprus

indicators.note: over says the noble's title is turned round

parts.note: a peer is a lord or other titled noble

explanation.surface: A sinister aristocrat is lurking in Cyprus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns the lord round to REEP; CY is the country's internet and vehicle code, a convention worth learning.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unsettling and menacing gives the shivers, much like sinister.

clue.text: Bakers working in North American state

indicators.note: in puts the reworked letters inside the abbreviation
working suggests the word Bakers is put to work in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Bakers busy at work somewhere in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North American state' looks like the whole definition, but 'North American' is wordplay; 'working' gives EBRASK.
explanation.definitionFit: This Great Plains territory is one of the fifty in the USA.

clue.text: Find a way around team on stage

parts.note: a side is a team
a step is a stage in a process

explanation.surface: A team on a stage finds a workaround.
explanation.definitionFit: To dodge or evade a problem is to avoid confronting it.

clue.text: Ship that is carrying good women's wear

indicators.note: carrying says the ship and its abbreviation hold a letter inside

parts.note: a liner is a large passenger ship
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A ship's cargo of quality clothing for women.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladies' underwear and nightclothes are a kind of women's clothing.

clue.text: Group from Ireland — vehicle shown in article, overturned

indicators.note: shown in puts the country and vehicle inside the flipped article
overturned says the article is flipped round

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
a van is a vehicle

explanation.surface: A band from Ireland whose van overturned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group' means a pop group, not a collection; 'overturned' applies to the article alone, giving NA.
explanation.definitionFit: The Seattle grunge band led by Kurt Cobain was a rock group.

clue.text: Rodent, second to appear in bazaar

indicators.note: to appear in places the short time inside the market

parts.note: a mart is a market or bazaar
a mo is a moment, a second

explanation.surface: A rodent makes a brief appearance at a market.
explanation.definitionFit: This burrowing mountain animal is a large ground squirrel, a type of rodent.

clue.text: Note what act has?

parts.note: the word act has its centre letter as one of the musical notes

explanation.surface: A theatre query about a note in an act.
explanation.walkthrough: The three-letter word act has C in the middle.
explanation.definitionFit: The C near the centre of a piano keyboard is a musical note.

clue.text: Irish novelist frowning on English

parts.note: stern means severe, frowning

explanation.surface: A writer from Ireland scowls at English.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence, author of Tristram Shandy, was born in Clonmel, Ireland.

clue.text: HQ's courage and heart

parts.note: nerve means courage or daring
the centre of something is its heart

explanation.surface: Headquarters needs bravery and a strong core.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', linking definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: The control hub of an organisation is its headquarters, from which it is run.

clue.text: Party time for Dorothy

parts.note: a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: It is time for Dorothy's party.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a common pet form of the given name Dorothy.

clue.text: Resolute biblical character, leader of army (NT)

parts.note: Adam is the first man in Genesis

indicators.note: leader of takes the first letter of army

explanation.surface: A determined figure from scripture leads an army in the New Testament.
explanation.walkthrough: NT, the New Testament abbreviation, is used as it stands.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone unshakeable and firm in their decision is resolute.

clue.text: Girl removing top is a fool

indicators.note: removing top means the word for girl loses its first letter

parts.note: a lass is a girl

explanation.surface: A girl taking off her top is being foolish.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey is a byword for a silly, stupid person.

clue.text: Typical long-standing customer

definitions.meaning: a habitual patron of a shop or pub

explanation.surface: A description of the usual sort of loyal customer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both normal or usual and a frequent patron who keeps returning.

clue.text: Deception of criminals taking in prelates abroad

indicators.note: taking in says the receivers hold the jumbled letters inside

parts.note: fences are criminals who deal in stolen goods

indicators.note: abroad suggests the word prelates is scattered widely into a new order

explanation.surface: Crooks have bishops among them in an overseas fraud.
explanation.walkthrough: A fence is slang for a receiver of stolen goods; 'abroad' scatters the churchmen into ALSEPRET.
explanation.definitionFit: Obtaining something by lying about facts is a legal term for fraud or trickery.
